title: Kingdom of Aksum
summary: Ancient state in northern Ethiopia, founded in the 1st century CE and flourishing from the 3rd to the 6th century, with Aksum as its capital. UNESCO calls it the most powerful state between the Eastern Roman Empire and Persia. Its king Ezana adopted Christianity in the mid-4th century; decline began in the 7th century.

uncertainty.note: WHE says founded in the 1st century CE (a single king united the kingdom in the late 1st century) and gone by the late 8th century; UNESCO speaks of political decline in the 10th century.

as_recorded.value: It was founded in the 1st century CE

importance.justification: A trading kingdom that minted its own coins and adopted Christianity, ranked by UNESCO as the most powerful state between the Eastern Roman Empire and Persia.

reviewer_note: End date is uncertain: WHE gives decline from the late 6th century and from the 7th century on the same page and an end in the late 8th; UNESCO places political decline in the 10th. The WHE page also reports the Aksumite sack of Meroë (Ezana, r. c. 303-350 CE), linked only by related. Specific dates of the 1st-century founding are not stated.
